findings.explanation: encryptCredential() uses a constant, hardcoded all-zero 12-byte IV for AES-256-GCM on every call instead of generating a fresh IV via crypto.randomBytes(12). Because the same (key, IV) pair is reused across every credential encrypted with a given master key, an attacker who obtains two ciphertexts can XOR them to recover the XOR of the plaintexts (keystream reuse), and GCM's authentication/integrity guarantee is broken entirely under nonce reuse (forgery becomes feasible via the GHASH collision). Fix: generate iv = crypto.randomBytes(12) per encryption call and store/encode it alongside the ciphertext (the code already stores ivPart in the envelope, so decryptCredential does not need to change).
